A_target.statement:
Let $T$ be a [[Definition:Consistent|consistent]], [[Definition:Recursively Axiomatized Theory|recursively axiomatized]] extension of [[Definition:Robinson Arithmetic|Robinson arithmetic]].
Then there is a sentence $G$ with $T 
vdash G$; and if $T$ proves only true $\Sigma_1$ sentences, then also $T 
vdash 
eg G$.

B_source.statement:
Let $\map B x$ be a formula with one free variable and $T$ extend Robinson arithmetic.
Then there is a sentence $G$ with $T \vdash G \leftrightarrow \map B {\ulcorner G \urcorner}$.

substitutions.the formula B: the negation of the provability predicate of T

derived.the diagonal sentence: a sentence asserting its own unprovability

object_map.reformulation: Diagonalize against provability rather than truth; the liar becomes a true but unprovable sentence.

validity_conditions: Recursive axiomatization makes provability expressible by a Sigma_1 formula.
Robinson arithmetic proves every true Sigma_1 sentence, which is used in the first half.
proof_plan:
Let $\map {\operatorname {Prov}_T} x$ be a $\Sigma_1$ formula expressing provability in $T$.
By the [[Diagonal Lemma]], there is $G$ with $T \vdash G \leftrightarrow \neg \map {\operatorname {Prov}_T} {\ulcorner G \urcorner}$.

If $T \vdash G$, then $\map {\operatorname {Prov}_T} {\ulcorner G \urcorner}$ is a true $\Sigma_1$ sentence, hence provable in $T$, so $T \vdash \neg G$ and $T$ is inconsistent.
Hence $T \nvdash G$.

If $T \vdash 
eg G$, then $T \vdash \map {\operatorname {Prov}_T} {\ulcorner G \urcorner}$, which is then true by $\Sigma_1$-soundness, so $T \vdash G$ and $T$ is inconsistent.
Hence $T 
vdash 
eg G$.
